headline: Dry through Wednesday everywhere. Small chances for an inch or two return Oct 22–26, best in the Canadian Rockies and Coast Mountains.
body: A split flow sends this week's storm into California, so all six spots stay dry through Wednesday, Oct 21; even the wettest ensemble members show under half an inch. Snow levels are high this morning, 7,000–9,600 ft across Washington. Weak systems Thursday through Monday (Oct 22–26) bring snow levels down to 2,500–4,500 ft, but consensus totals are only 0.1–1.1 in. The best odds of at least an inch are at Banff Sunshine (71%) and Whistler (49%). The GFS still shows a major storm Oct 26–28, putting about 50 in at Crystal by Oct 31, but ECMWF (1–4 in) and the ensembles don't support it.
watch: Whether ECMWF or the ensembles pick up the GFS storm for Oct 26–28.

headline: Dry through Wednesday. Maybe a wet dusting Saturday, Oct 24, and nothing bigger supported yet.
body: Mid-mountain is near 40°F this morning with the snow level around 9,600 ft and gusts to 35 mph. Every model is dry for the next five days. For Oct 22–26 the consensus is 0.9 in (ensemble range 0–1.3 in, 15% chance of 1 in or more), mostly Saturday, Oct 24 as the snow level drops to about 3,750 ft, then near 2,250 ft on Sunday. The GFS piles up about 50 in by Oct 31, against roughly 3 in on ECMWF and a 15-day ensemble median of 1.9 in.
watch: Snow level falling below base (4,400 ft) Oct 24–25, and any shift toward the GFS storm.

headline: Dry and mild. Snow levels stay above the pass until late on Monday, Oct 26.
body: 45°F at the upper lifts this morning with the snow level near 7,650 ft. Dry through Wednesday. Snow levels sit at 4,100–5,350 ft through the weekend, above the 3,000 ft base, and only reach it Monday night, Oct 26. Consensus for Oct 22–26 is 0.1 in with a 12% chance of an inch. The GFS shows about 32 in by Oct 31, but ECMWF has about 1 in.
watch: Monday night, Oct 26, when the snow level first reaches pass level.

headline: Dry through Wednesday, then light snow chances above 4,000 ft Oct 22–26.
body: 37°F at Heather Pass with a 7,000 ft snow level this morning. NWS Spokane expects dry weather through midweek, then Cascade-crest showers of only a few hundredths from Thursday, with snow levels near 4,000–5,000 ft. Consensus for Oct 22–26 is 0.7 in (range 0–3.1 in), with a 29% chance of 1 in or more and 6% for 6 in. The GFS shows about 23 in by Oct 31 versus about 3 in on ECMWF.
watch: A colder end to October would raise the odds of an early Highway 20 winter closure.

headline: A coin flip for an inch at the Roundhouse Oct 22–26, with a wide range behind it.
body: Right at freezing on the upper mountain and 45°F in the village this morning, with the snow level near 4,750 ft. Nothing meaningful through Wednesday. From Thursday the snow level drops to 3,000–4,200 ft, keeping the village wet, and the consensus is 0.9 in with an ensemble range of 0–5.4 in (49% chance of 1 in, 10% chance of 6 in). Over 15 days the ensemble median is 5.6 in, with a 90th percentile of 25 in.
watch: Monday night, Oct 26, the snowiest period in the current runs.

headline: Dry this week. Light snow returns to the upper mountain Oct 23–26, with the models in rough agreement.
body: 35°F at mid-mountain this morning. Nothing through Wednesday. Consensus for Oct 22–26 is 0.5 in (range 0–3.7 in, 33% chance of 1 in), with snow levels dipping to 2,650–3,350 ft at times. The models agree better here than further west: by Oct 30–31 the GFS shows 5 in, ECMWF 3.9 in and the ensemble median 3 in.
watch: Friday night, Oct 23, and Monday night, Oct 26.

headline: Best odds of fresh snow among the six: about an inch Friday, Oct 23.
body: 34°F at the village this morning. Dry through Wednesday. Friday, Oct 23 is the best chance: about 0.6 in during the day and 0.2 in overnight, ensemble up to 1.7 in. Consensus for Oct 22–26 is 1.1 in (range 0.3–4.7 in), with a 71% chance of at least an inch. Over 15 days ECMWF (5.2 in) is slightly snowier than the GFS (2.4 in).
